subject: VPC connectivity - next steps for FinPay integration
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: VPC connectivity - next steps for FinPay integration

Hi Alex / Priya

Thanks again for the call today great to meet the FinPay team. Quick recap and proposed next steps re: private connectivity and auth so we can scope the Dedicated deployment and plan the POC: 

Summary from our call:
- Goal: Integrate Redwood Private with FinPay VPC for inference serving (embeddings + reranking + model routing) with strict egress controls.
- Requirements you mentioned: VPC endpoints or NAT egress with IP allowlisting, DNS resolution for Redwood endpoints, mTLS between FinPay and our dedicated proxy, and SSO-based service auth for SDK tokens.
- Constraints: Compliance wants cert rotation plan, and netops prefers IP allowlist over opening wide CIDR ranges.

Proposed next steps (we can run these in parallel):
1) Network diagram + IP list: Marissa to share our expected outbound IPs and endpoints for the VPC endpoints option. FinPay netops to confirm if they can create an interface endpoint or prefer allowlist.
2) mTLS checklist: Jonas to document the TLS handshake/cert expectations and cert rotation process.
3) SDK/auth: I'll share our SDK quickstart + how we do token-based auth with short-lived tokens and optional vault/KMS integration.
4) POC plan: If netops can provide a staging VPC or allowlist, we'll run a 2-week POC with embeddings and a small reranker model.

Can you confirm who from FinPay netops will own the endpoint creation and a good time window next week for a short tech-sync (30m)?

Attachments: draft network diagram + mTLS checklist for reference.

Thanks
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@finpay.com>, FinPay Networking Team <netops@finpay.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC connectivity - next steps for FinPay integration

Hi Lauren

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 
- Netops lead: Priya Natarajan will own the endpoint work. She's looped here.
- Preferred approach: We prefer VPC Interface Endpoints for tighter control, but we'll need the concrete list of FQDNs + service ports you require. IP allowlist is acceptable as a fallback for staging.
- mTLS: We can handle client certs issued by our internal CA; need your cert requirements (key size, renew cadence).
- Auth: We use HashiCorp Vault for service secrets; short-lived tokens are preferred. Can your SDK integrate with Vault or do you support exchanging Vault-issued creds for Redwood tokens?

Can Priya and I book a 30m tech sync Thursday morning (Mar 31) at 9:00 PT?

Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product Engineering | FinPay
alex.chen@finpay.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@finpay.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 07:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC connectivity - next steps for FinPay integration

Thanks Alex / Priya

I've attached a short mTLS checklist and our expected TLS parameters: RSA 2048 or ECDSA P-256 accepted, certs must include SANs for the proxy FQDNs, and we recommend 30-day rotation for client certs during POC (we support longer in production). For the interface endpoint flow we need:

- Outbound FQDNs for the Redwood private control plane and runtime (I've included them in the attached diagram).
- Ports: 443 for API/streaming; 8443 if you choose a separate mTLS proxy port.

On Vault integration: Redwood supports token exchange flows. Typical approach: FinPay issues a short-lived machine token via Vault to the application; the application hits our /auth/exchange endpoint (mutual TLS) to mint a Redwood session token with a TTL you control. If you prefer, we can demo the flow in the POC.

For the tech sync 9:00 PT tomorrow works for me. I'll bring a short checklist to validate during the call.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Perfect thanks all. Confirming the 9:00 PT tech sync today. Agenda (15-20m):
- Quick intros + ownership
- Confirm interface endpoint vs allowlist for POC
- mTLS parameters & cert owner/rotation
- Auth/token exchange approach and any Vault constraints
- Success criteria for 2-week POC (embeddings + reranker latency + secure egress)

Marissa can you drop the outbound FQDNs and the network diagram into the Drive link before the call? I've also flagged the HubSpot deal so our AE can track progress (HS-12345).

See you all shortly
Lauren
